The ACTUAL task is to implement a bidirectional Python daemon that reads Braydon's handwritten Supernote notes into paia-work/folio and enables PAIA agents to write .note pages. The INFERRED task describes discovery/analysis work: examining existing codebase, checking utilities, and assessing gaps. While both concern paia-supernote, they represent fundamentally different work streams. The inferred task appears to be preparatory groundwork rather than the core implementation objective. Semantic alignment is low because actual specifies concrete deliverables (daemon, bidirectional sync) while inferred reconstructs exploratory activities. Requirement coverage is partial: understanding the codebase could support implementation, but the inferred task doesn't address any of the actual read/write functionality requirements. Specificity is similarly mismatched—actual is concrete (daemon, note pages, specific integrations), inferred is generic (assess, identify gaps). Most of the inferred task's content (codebase analysis, component identification, gap assessment) is not present in the original specification.
